openResidualsFromTheFinalReview.summary: A config-change transaction that alters window_seconds and does not commit promptly holds the EXCLUSIVE advisory lock and freezes every guest admission for as long as it stays open. No timeout anywhere.
openResidualsFromTheFinalReview.scope: Requires a raw SQL connection, i.e. an actor already inside the trusted-operator boundary.
openResidualsFromTheFinalReview.impact: Availability only. No data corruption, no limiter bypass, no privilege escalation, fully recoverable by ending the transaction.

openResidualsFromTheFinalReview.summary: The advisory key is a bare integer visible in source, and pg_advisory_xact_lock/_shared are PUBLIC-executable, so any role with a raw SQL connection can trigger the same freeze without holding a single grant in the limiter schema - bypassing the migration's REVOKE ALL discipline.
openResidualsFromTheFinalReview.scope: Raw-SQL-connection actors only. pg_advisory_xact_lock lives in pg_catalog and is NOT reachable as a PostgREST RPC, so anon and authenticated cannot reach it through the application surface.

openResidualsFromTheFinalReview.summary: No acceptance test races an admission against a concurrent config change. r5 recommended one and it was not added, so the fix's correctness rests on ad hoc reproduction rather than anything CI would catch on regression.
openResidualsFromTheFinalReview.impact: Test-coverage gap, not a behavioural defect.
